I'd give it a solid 86%, great game. Has an interesting story, mechanics are fun and intense, certain events\missions get your adrenaline pumping. The soundtrack really fits in with what's happening and there are lots of fun easter-eggs, like the [spoiler] Gaping Dragon [/spoiler] and the [spoiler] Clock [/spoiler], or all the interesting IRC chat prints which take you back to the good ole' days of internet chatting.

The devs seem pretty cool too, letting you know how the game works so you can make your own "extension" mods, and it, SOMEHOW, still manages to find some replayability. I've only just finished my first solo playthrough and I thorougly enjoyed it. Only one thing ground my gears still: I felt lost playing the game sometimes - I didn't know what to do because the mission objectives weren't THAT clear, in some very specific cases. I also think that while some side-missions 
or "contracts" are interesting, others seem very easy or boring to do, especially after performing the hardest ones. If there is a "sequence" to it I'm not sure if I followed it.

Overall a great game, and at a cheap price too. Would recommend to everyone who likes puzzles or enigmas or just something to toy with their brains. It's surprisingly challenging and intense too.

Intro - Absolutely amazing game!

Just finished playing through the whole game (including Labyrinths DLC) for the second time! This game is VERY in depth -- you will get intrenched into the story. Everything is incrediably detailed. Detail - Highly Recommended, but be careful of some passwords (some look like 1 but is a lowercase L, and double check your password if you get stuck. Conclusion - Amazing game, rated "T" for a reason, worth every penny.

I bought the game on sale thinking it'd be a nice little fun time waster for the Memorial Day Weekend. Nothing special.

Boy was I wrong!

I underestimated this little Indie Gem (and that is EXACTLY  what is this game is: a gem) I was immediately hooked and I spent every waking hour of that weekend playing just Hacknet. The story was a little "meh", but Hacknet's one of those games where it's acceptable because the real focus is about the gameplay and mechanics. This game is ROCK SOLID when it comes to those two things.

This game is often compared to Uplink, but Hacknet NAILS the realistic features in its game. You type actual real-life UNIX/Linux commands into a terminal to get stuff done in Hacknet. You can't get fancy with the command line, but that didn't take away the thrill. To me, that was very cool.

This game contains little nuggets of comedy from http://Bash.org, so be on the look out for those IRC logs stored on many computers in-game!

Would I recommend this game? YES. 

I give this Indie GEM a solid 8/10 and it's definitely worth your money.

Simply put, it is a very well put together game…end of.

You start by simply hacking into insecure computers and retrieving trivial information, but by the end of it, your hacking into the most secure computer in the game, while the computer you are hacking is trying to eliminate your computer. 

Each puzzle can be repetitive which could be a problem for some people, but I found that I really enjoyed those sorts of puzzles, especially hunting for passwords and hacking security. The only other negative I could possibly say is that when a tracer gets your computer’s IP in game, it displays a blue screen, which I initially thought was my actual computer crashing, which was a bit scary.

The story line is really well told and I thoroughly enjoyed it. While the one mission where you COULD euthanise a person (you do not have to accept this mission) was a bit touchy for some people, the rest of the missions flowed nicely, and the final mission was hard but enjoyable to the fullest. The ending was very well executed overall and a good finish to the game.

The soundtracks really complement the game and give the game a full immersive feeling, and I can really appreciate the artistic talent of the people who created them. Likewise, the art to go with it is equally as impressive, and the UI represents a hacker-like environment.

The game itself is surprising accurate to real life hacking, with all of the port numbers corresponding to real port numbers in modern computing as well as their respective protocol.

Overall, it is an easily amazing and fun game, and am glad there is DLC to go with this, as I simply cannot get enough of this game!

Hacknet is far more fun and engaging than a game about imputing command line instructions has any right to be.  While it's neither very long nor complex it contains the simple joy of a game with a solid learning curve and enough challenge to make winning feel like an accomplishment.

While it is very much "Hollywood Hacking" as opposed to the real deal, that also makes it more accessible to the majority of players.  And, ultimately, even that concession serves the story that is buried within your actions.  There's a reason simple commands and a few modules are so powerful and it's a terrifying one.

Exactly long enough to explore its ideas and exactly deep enough for a pleasent afternoon of fun, Hacknet is worth the price in my book.

Hacknet is a puzzling mystery game where you take on the role of a hacker who must contribute to the computing world of hackers by breaking into systems with the use of special programs, navigate and modify files and data in such systems, and complete tasks for other people on the behalf of your faction. The game features the usage of actual terminal commands and coding in order to navigate the complex game, forcing the player to learn and adapt to the usage of this code quickly in order to press forward in game. The ultimate goal of the player is to discover the fate of a mysterious, experienced hacker that goes by the name of 'Bit', who helps out the player at the beginning on the game, allowing them to get up on their feet and stand a fighting chance against the brutal world of code.

The game is a decent length. For a slow gamer who wishes to experience and explore, this game usually takes ~15 hours to complete. Some quick cookies may find that they can complete the main story in as little as 5 hours, however.

Whether I recommend this to every player or not is quite trivial. An almost definite prerequisite for playing this game is the excellent ability to problem solve, and the capability to explore. This game isn't for every player out there, as there is certainly the possibility of frustration and boredom when the player cannot figure out what direction they should take or how to correctly solve one of the many challenging puzzles the game has to offer. For those that love to code and adore solving complex, challenging problems, this game is definitely a buy. If you see the game on sale grab it real quick!
